prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1412; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a report of a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. Insured vehicle was stopped at the light when struck from behind by the third-party vehicle. Police report requested. Claimant reports neck pain and stiffness and has not yet sought medical treatment. Claimant is not represented by counsel at this time.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant by phone. Claimant describes immediate neck stiffness with headaches developing later that evening. Claimant is currently seeing their family physician and has provided a preliminary note confirming a diagnosis of whiplash-type cervical strain. Reviewed the scene photos from the insured's submission; rear bumper damage is visible and consistent with the reported impact speed.

Entry 3: Obtained the police report. Responding officer documented the third-party driver's admission of being distracted at the time of impact. Liability appears clear. Advised claimant by letter of the claims process and of the right to seek independent advice. Claimant has not yet indicated whether they intend to retain a lawyer.

Entry 4: Received medical records from the claimant's physician covering the initial examination and a physiotherapy referral. Records note reduced range of motion in the cervical spine and ongoing complaints of intermittent headaches. Treatment plan calls for a course of physiotherapy over several weeks. Reviewing records against the reported mechanism of injury; no inconsistencies noted so far.

Entry 5: Claimant called to ask about the timeline for settlement and how medical expenses are handled while treatment is ongoing. Explained the general steps and that a final evaluation will wait until treatment is complete and records are current. Scheduled a follow-up call in two weeks to review progress and update the file. Claimant remains unrepresented.
